scope: Retail .aid route network for the primary raced route of amboy, gracia and river. Each route is the ordered racing-line polyline (line index 5) of the retail AITrackDataRoutes record, with arc length, serialized width and serialized racing-line offset per segment. Every retail pickup of probes/powerups/data/runtime-placement.json is projected onto the network. No coordinate, width or offset is synthesized.

formatAuthority.decoder: probes/course/tools/aid_decode.py (read-only reference; this builder re-implements it)

coordinateRule: segment origin = (xFile, -zFile); segment lateral normal = normalize(tangentX, -tangentZ); line k position = origin + normal * width * line[k].offset; line k y = line[k].height. Matches AITrackDataSegments::GetPositionFromOffset (trackdata.h:477-490).
projectionRule: A pickup is on-route when it falls inside at least one engine segment quad (AITrackDataSegments::GetSegmentBounds / InSegmentWidths, trackdata.h:1055-1122): lateral offset in [0, 1] * width and longitudinal offset in [-2, +2] m around a 4 m sample. `containingRoutes` lists every route whose corridor contains the pickup, narrowest first. `route`/`routeIndex`/`segment`/`arc`/`offset`/`lateral`/`width`/`along` describe the most specific carrier (narrowest containing corridor, then nearest racing line, then lowest route index). distanceToRouteNetwork is the planar distance to the nearest racing-line polyline of the whole route network; distanceToAssignedRacingLine is the planar distance to the assigned route only; distanceToCorridor is 0 inside the assigned quad. arc is the assigned route racing-line arc at the projected station.

tolerances.note: corridorMetres is numerical slack on the engine quad test; the retail slots are genuinely inside the corridor, not snapped to it.
